meta.title: Language Skills & Subskills
meta.randomizationRule: Randomize question selection/order and answer-option order on every attempt; never reuse an exact attempt signature.
meta.alignment: TKT Module 1 — Describing language and language skills: reading, listening, speaking, writing, their subskills, and features of spoken/written texts

questions.prompt: Learners read a newspaper article quickly to understand the main idea. Which subskill are they mainly using?
questions.explanation: Reading for gist means reading to understand the general meaning or main idea.

questions.prompt: A learner reads a webpage rapidly to get a general impression of its content. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Skimming means reading quickly to get a general idea of a text.

questions.prompt: Before reading an article titled “Why We Sleep”, learners guess what information it may contain. Which subskill are they using?
questions.explanation: Predicting uses clues such as titles, visuals and prior knowledge to anticipate content.

questions.prompt: Which task best practises reading for gist?
options: Choose the best title for the whole article
Find the date of the event
questions.correctAnswer: Choose the best title for the whole article
questions.explanation: Choosing an overall title requires understanding the general meaning of the text.

questions.prompt: What is the main relationship between skimming and reading for gist?
options: Skimming is a technique often used to achieve gist understanding
Reading for gist means locating one exact fact
questions.correctAnswer: Skimming is a technique often used to achieve gist understanding
questions.explanation: Skimming describes fast reading; gist describes the overall understanding the reader is trying to obtain.

questions.prompt: Learners have 30 seconds to read four short texts and match each one to a heading. Which subskill is primarily being tested?
questions.explanation: Matching headings requires understanding the overall meaning of each text.

questions.prompt: Which instruction most clearly encourages skimming?
options: Read quickly and decide what the text is mainly about
Find the exact price mentioned in paragraph 3
questions.correctAnswer: Read quickly and decide what the text is mainly about
questions.explanation: Skimming involves fast reading for general meaning.

questions.prompt: A teacher shows only the title and photograph before learners read. Which subskill is the teacher most likely activating?
questions.explanation: Titles and visuals provide clues that readers can use to anticipate text content.

questions.prompt: Which task is least suitable for practising gist reading?
options: Find every example of the past perfect
Decide which headline matches the article
questions.correctAnswer: Find every example of the past perfect
questions.explanation: Finding every example of a form requires close reading rather than gist reading.

questions.prompt: Which distinction between skimming and scanning is correct?
options: Skimming is for general meaning; scanning is for specific information
Skimming is for grammar; scanning is for pronunciation
questions.correctAnswer: Skimming is for general meaning; scanning is for specific information
questions.explanation: Skimming seeks an overview; scanning searches selectively for particular information.

questions.prompt: A learner looks through a timetable to find the departure time of one train. Which subskill is this?
questions.explanation: Scanning means searching a text for specific information.

questions.prompt: Learners read a paragraph carefully to identify three reasons given by the writer. Which subskill are they using?
questions.explanation: Reading for detail means reading carefully to understand specific information.

questions.prompt: A learner guesses the meaning of “exhausted” from the surrounding sentence. Which subskill is this?
questions.explanation: The learner uses surrounding language and meaning to work out an unfamiliar word.

questions.prompt: A text never says the writer is annoyed, but the language strongly suggests irritation. Which subskill is needed?
questions.explanation: Inference involves understanding meaning that is implied rather than directly stated.

questions.prompt: Which task most clearly requires scanning rather than reading for detail?
options: Explain why the writer changed jobs
questions.explanation: Scanning is used to locate a specific item of information quickly.

questions.prompt: Learners search a long webpage for the registration deadline. Which subskill are they mainly using?
questions.explanation: They are searching selectively for one specific piece of information.

questions.prompt: Which question most clearly tests reading for detail?
options: What two problems did the author experience on the journey?
What is the text generally about?
What do you think the article may discuss?
questions.correctAnswer: What two problems did the author experience on the journey?
questions.explanation: Answering requires careful understanding of specific information.

questions.prompt: The writer calls a failed proposal “another brilliant idea from management”. Which subskill helps the reader recognise possible sarcasm?
questions.explanation: The reader must interpret attitude from context rather than literal words alone.

questions.prompt: Which activity practises deducing meaning from context?
options: Work out an unknown word using the sentences around it
Look up every unknown word before reading
questions.correctAnswer: Work out an unknown word using the sentences around it
questions.explanation: Contextual clues can help readers infer the meaning of unfamiliar vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes scanning from reading for detail?
options: Scanning searches selectively for a target; reading for detail processes information more thoroughly
Reading for detail means reading only headings
questions.correctAnswer: Scanning searches selectively for a target; reading for detail processes information more thoroughly
questions.explanation: Scanning is selective, while detailed reading involves closer processing of relevant information.

questions.prompt: Learners listen once to understand the general topic of a conversation. Which subskill are they using?
questions.explanation: Listening for gist focuses on overall meaning.

questions.prompt: Learners listen for a flight number in an airport announcement. Which subskill are they mainly using?
questions.explanation: The listener focuses on one target item of information.

questions.prompt: Learners listen carefully to identify exactly why a speaker missed an appointment. Which subskill is being practised?
questions.explanation: The task requires careful understanding of specific information.

questions.prompt: A speaker never says “I'm angry”, but tone and wording show strong irritation. Which listening subskill is required?
questions.explanation: The listener interprets meaning that is implied rather than explicitly stated.

questions.prompt: Before hearing a restaurant conversation, learners predict vocabulary and topics they may hear. Which subskill is being activated?
questions.explanation: Prediction uses context and prior knowledge to anticipate content.

questions.prompt: Which task most clearly practises listening for gist?
options: Decide whether the speakers are discussing work, travel or health
questions.correctAnswer: Decide whether the speakers are discussing work, travel or health
questions.explanation: The task focuses on the overall topic rather than details.

questions.prompt: Learners listen repeatedly to a short extract and identify exact words and pronunciation features. What type of listening is this?
questions.explanation: Intensive listening involves close, focused attention to a relatively short stretch of speech.

questions.prompt: Which question mainly tests inference in listening?
options: How does the speaker probably feel about the decision?
What time does the train leave?
questions.correctAnswer: How does the speaker probably feel about the decision?
questions.explanation: The listener must interpret an attitude or feeling that may not be directly stated.

questions.prompt: A teacher pauses a recording and asks learners what they expect to hear next. Which subskill is being practised?
questions.explanation: Learners use what they have already heard to anticipate subsequent content.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between listening for gist and listening for detail?
options: Gist focuses on overall meaning; detail focuses on specific information and relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Gist focuses on overall meaning; detail focuses on specific information and relationships
questions.explanation: The two subskills differ mainly in depth and focus of comprehension.

questions.prompt: A learner keeps a conversation going by asking follow-up questions and responding to the other speaker. Which subskill is this?
questions.explanation: Interactive strategies help speakers initiate, maintain and manage interaction.

questions.prompt: A learner explains the main points of a long discussion in a shorter form. Which subskill is this?
questions.explanation: Summarising means expressing the main points in a shorter form.

questions.prompt: A learner cannot remember “thermometer”, so says “the thing you use to measure temperature”. Which subskill is this?
questions.explanation: Paraphrasing means expressing the same idea in different words.

questions.prompt: A learner speaks smoothly with few unnatural pauses, although some grammar mistakes remain. Which feature is strongest?
questions.explanation: Fluency concerns smooth and efficient communication.

questions.prompt: A learner produces grammatically correct sentences but pauses for a long time before almost every phrase. Which description is best?
options: Accuracy is strong; fluency is weak
Fluency is strong; accuracy is weak
questions.correctAnswer: Accuracy is strong; fluency is weak
questions.explanation: Accuracy concerns correctness; fluency concerns flow and ease of communication.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour best illustrates an interactive strategy?
options: Asking for clarification when something is unclear
Looking for a date in a text
questions.correctAnswer: Asking for clarification when something is unclear
questions.explanation: Clarification requests help speakers manage interaction.

questions.prompt: A learner says, “In other words, the project was delayed because...” Which subskill is the learner using?
questions.explanation: The learner is reformulating an idea using different wording.

questions.prompt: Which task primarily develops summarising in speaking?
options: Listen to a three-minute report and give the main points in thirty seconds
questions.correctAnswer: Listen to a three-minute report and give the main points in thirty seconds
questions.explanation: The speaker must select and restate the main information briefly.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes fluency?
options: The ability to communicate relatively smoothly and efficiently
The absence of every grammatical error
The visual organisation of a written text
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to communicate relatively smoothly and efficiently
questions.explanation: Fluency focuses on flow and ease of communication rather than perfect correctness.

questions.prompt: A speaking activity asks learners to focus on correct verb endings and precise pronunciation rather than speed. Which feature is being prioritised?
questions.explanation: Accuracy concerns correct language use, including grammar, vocabulary and pronunciation.

questions.prompt: A learner checks a finished email for spelling, punctuation and grammar mistakes. Which subskill is this?
questions.explanation: Proofreading means checking a near-final text for surface-level errors.

questions.prompt: A learner changes the order of two paragraphs because the ideas are not logically organised. Which process is this?
questions.explanation: Editing involves improving content, organisation or language in a draft.

questions.prompt: A learner reduces a 500-word article to a 100-word version containing only the key ideas. Which subskill is being used?
questions.explanation: Summarising involves selecting and expressing the main ideas concisely.

questions.prompt: A learner rewrites “The results were surprising” as “The findings were unexpected.” Which subskill does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Paraphrasing expresses the same or a similar meaning using different language.

questions.prompt: What is the clearest difference between proofreading and editing?
options: Proofreading checks errors in a near-final text; editing may involve larger changes to content and organisation
questions.correctAnswer: Proofreading checks errors in a near-final text; editing may involve larger changes to content and organisation
questions.explanation: Editing can involve substantial revision; proofreading usually focuses on final surface accuracy.

questions.prompt: Which activity most directly practises proofreading?
options: Find and correct spelling and punctuation errors in a final draft
Choose the best title for an article
questions.correctAnswer: Find and correct spelling and punctuation errors in a final draft
questions.explanation: Proofreading focuses on detecting and correcting surface errors.

questions.prompt: Which activity is mainly editing rather than proofreading?
options: Remove an irrelevant paragraph and improve the order of ideas
questions.correctAnswer: Remove an irrelevant paragraph and improve the order of ideas
questions.explanation: Editing includes decisions about relevance, organisation and clarity.

questions.prompt: Which task best practises paraphrasing?
options: Rewrite a sentence using different words but keep the meaning
Find the phone number in a text
questions.correctAnswer: Rewrite a sentence using different words but keep the meaning
questions.explanation: Paraphrasing preserves meaning while changing wording or structure.

questions.prompt: Which task best practises summarising?
options: Write the three main points of a long text in one short paragraph
List every example in the text
questions.correctAnswer: Write the three main points of a long text in one short paragraph
questions.explanation: Summarising selects essential information and presents it concisely.

questions.prompt: A learner has excellent grammar but the ideas in an essay appear in a confusing order. Which feature most needs improvement?
questions.explanation: Written texts need clear logical organisation as well as accurate language.

questions.prompt: Headings, paragraphs, bullet points and columns are examples of which text feature?
questions.explanation: Layout refers to the visual arrangement of a written text.

questions.prompt: A real restaurant menu used unchanged in a language lesson is best described as:
questions.explanation: Authentic texts are created for real-world communication rather than specifically for language teaching.

questions.prompt: A spoken presentation has a clear introduction, development and conclusion. Which feature is being described?
questions.explanation: Organisation concerns how ideas and sections are structured coherently.

questions.prompt: A learner's written text contains almost no grammatical or spelling errors. Which feature is particularly strong?
questions.explanation: Accuracy refers to correct use of language.

questions.prompt: Why might an authentic text be challenging for learners?
options: It was created for real users and may contain language not simplified for learners
It must always be grammatically incorrect
questions.correctAnswer: It was created for real users and may contain language not simplified for learners
questions.explanation: Authentic texts reflect real communication and may contain complex or unfamiliar language.

questions.prompt: Which feature is most directly concerned with how information is visually arranged on a page?
questions.explanation: Layout includes visual features such as headings, columns, paragraphs and spacing.

questions.prompt: A podcast episode produced for the general public and used unchanged in class is:
questions.explanation: It was created for a real-world audience rather than specifically for language learning.

questions.prompt: Which pair best contrasts accuracy and fluency?
questions.explanation: Accuracy concerns correctness; fluency concerns flow and ease of communication.

questions.prompt: A text has accurate grammar but jumps randomly from one idea to another. Which feature is weakest?
questions.explanation: The problem is how ideas are structured and connected, not grammatical correctness.

questions.prompt: Which statement about authenticity is most accurate?
options: Authenticity concerns whether a text or task reflects real-world language use or purpose
Authentic texts must always be difficult
Authenticity is another term for grammatical accuracy
questions.correctAnswer: Authenticity concerns whether a text or task reflects real-world language use or purpose
questions.explanation: In ELT, authenticity relates to real-world sources, purposes or language use rather than simply difficulty.

matchingSets.instruction: Match each classroom task with the main subskill it practises.

items.example: Choose the best title for the article.
Find the departure time in the timetable.
Use the headline to guess what the article will discuss.
Decide how the speaker probably feels.
Check a final draft for spelling and punctuation errors.
Express the same idea using different words.

matchingSets.instruction: Match each description with the correct language-skill term.

items.example: Read rapidly to get an overview.
Ask for clarification and keep a conversation going.
Give only the main points in a shorter form.
Use a real-world text created for genuine communication.
